About

I am a software engineer focused on AI agent systems and developer infrastructure. My work spans agent runtimes, workflow orchestration, context engineering, and the infrastructure that supports reliable services.

From 2022 to 2026, I worked as a Software Development Engineer II in the WCX group at Microsoft, building infrastructure SDKs, cross-service authentication flows, and integration testing tools. Alongside this role, I was a core architect for Workfx AI, a part-time technical project, where I helped build an agent platform from the ground up and led two major architecture transitions.

Previously, I interned at ByteDance AI Lab, developing backend services for a speech training platform. I received my bachelor’s degree from Beijing Forestry University in 2022, where I led the ACM competitive programming team.

Selected Engineering

Workfx AI — Agent Platform & Harness Architecture

Core Architect · Part-time technical project · Mar 2023 – Jun 2026

I worked across the frontend, backend, AI services, and deployment infrastructure, with primary responsibility for the agent runtime, workflow orchestration, tool integration, and RAG pipeline. The work involved two major architecture transitions.

  1. From a ReAct chatbot to an agent-building platform. Evolved the original application to support both workflow-based and prompt-based agent authoring. The platform exposed configurable RAG, tools and skills, computer use, memory, human intervention, and scheduled triggers.
  2. From workflow-defined agents to a dedicated harness. Rebuilt a vertical GEO agent around a custom runtime, state machine, middleware, and context-management layer. This architecture supported input/output guardrails, memory and context compaction, recovery from stalled execution, multi-agent orchestration, and evaluation.

Microsoft WCX — Service Infrastructure & Testing

Software Development Engineer II · Jun 2022 – Aug 2026

  • WCX Infra SDK. Helped design and implement shared .NET middleware and Azure SDK wrappers for authentication, configuration, logging, and retries. The SDK provided a consistent integration layer for 60+ services across 40+ engineering teams.
  • Cross-service authentication. Independently owned the design and maintenance of WCX authentication flows, addressing compatibility across authentication chains, cross-service reliability, and consistent permission checks.
  • SIT integration testing framework. Developed a framework using topological sorting and dynamic programming to express tests with complex dependencies through JSON configuration, reducing test maintenance costs by 90%.
